fjord.sense: noun: A long, narrow, deep inlet between cliffs.

fjordlike.sense: adj: Resembling or characteristic of a fjord.
fjordlike.hook: Made from fjord + -like. fjord goes back to Proto-Indo-European *pértus, meaning "crossing".

fjeld.sense: noun: A rocky, barren plateau, especially in Scandinavia.

firstUse.quote: Almost every Norwegian farmer possesses some pasture-land high up in the fjeld, sometimes as much as twenty or thirty miles distant from his homestead.
firstUse.source: 1847, Alfred Smith, Henry Warren, “A SEATER COTTAGE ON THE FILLE FJELD”, in Sketches in Norway and Sweden, London: Thomas Maclean, via National Library of Norwa

fjordic.hook: Made from fjord + -ic. fjord goes back to Proto-Indo-European *pértus, meaning "crossing".

fjard.sense: noun: A more or less open body of water in a coastal archipelago.

fjordless.hook: Made from fjord + -less. fjord goes back to Proto-Indo-European *pértus, meaning "crossing".

fjardic.hook: Made from fjard + -ic. fjard goes back to Swedish fjärd.

fjordhead.sense: noun: The innermost part of a fjord.
fjordhead.hook: Wiktionary gives no earlier form for this sense.

fjordal.hook: Made from fjord + -al. fjord goes back to Proto-Indo-European *pértus, meaning "crossing".
